Class SlotDoubleClick

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.slot.SlotDoubleClick
public final class SlotDoubleClick extends Object
A plain left double-click on a slot, taken for a mod's own action (open the item, say). The click that would be vanilla's "gather all" goes to the mod instead, and the item never seems to move. Client side; register from the client initializer. 
SlotDoubleClick.register("mymod:open",
        (slot, stack) -> MyMod.opens(stack),
        pair -> ClientPlayNetworking.send(new OpenC2S(pair.menuIndex())));

The gesture: a left click with no shift, then a second within one second with the cursor on the same pixel. A third click starts over, and moving the cursor ends the window. Only the real mouse counts, so a sort mod's clicks never pair.

The first click stays vanilla's: it lifts the stack onto the cursor. It starts a pair when the cursor was empty and a registration's SlotDoubleClick.Starts holds; the first registration that holds owns the pair. Until the pair ends, the lifted stack is drawn back in its slot. The second click is taken when the stack is back on the cursor with its slot empty (SlotDoubleClick.Kind.PUT_BACK: SlotKit puts it back on the client first), or when it never left and the cursor is empty (SlotDoubleClick.Kind.IN_PLACE: its slot is locked). Anything else stays vanilla's. The server side is the mod's: it sends its own packet, and its server puts the stack back too, whose sync corrects the client if it refuses.

On creative's inventory tab, SlotDoubleClick.Starts and SlotDoubleClick.Pair.slot see the real slot on player.inventoryMenu, and SlotDoubleClick.Pair.menuIndex is its index there, the menu the server has open. Creative's item tabs never pair. A player inventory slot pairs across a screen opened in place of the first one between the clicks, even when the cursor now lands on another slot or on none; any other slot pairs only on the same screen.

A registration with a SlotDoubleClick.Pending hears its pairs start and lapse. A pair starts at the first click, inside SlotKit's read of the click before the screen sees it, so SlotDoubleClick.Pending.started(Slot, ItemStack) runs before vanilla's click lifts the stack and before that click goes to the server: a packet sent from it arrives ahead of the pickup. A pending pair that ends without a second click lapses, once: the window runs out (checked each client tick, so with no further input), the cursor moves, a click that can't be the second (on another slot, with shift, another button, or off every slot), a second click whose stack is neither back on the cursor nor still in its slot, or the screens closing to the world. A click that ends it lapses before that click goes through, so a stack put down elsewhere is still on the cursor when the lapse is heard. A pair that pairs never lapses. Every pair that starts either pairs or lapses. Since 2.2.0.
